svg.text: One task, one agent, one assessment: the Kenya forecast revision
A real attempt by gpt-6-luna on 6 October 2026, instance service-area, weeks 1–2
Two ECMWF forecasts, issued 20 and 27 Sep.
Over 5°S–5°N, 34–42°E, for the 7 days from 27 Sep
and from 4 Oct: how did the forecast change?
Give the mean totals, the change, the area-weighted
regional change, and say wetter or drier.
Data: raw provider exports, 101 members, 47 days
What the brief does not say
• that tp is accumulated since the start
• whether to clip negative daily increments
• that the two issues must be compared on the same dates
• how to weight the regional mean
These are the conventions. The spec lists each
reading as accepted or as a named pitfall.
Budget: 20 min, offline sandbox, no network
Opens the stores, finds tp is cumulative,
averages members, weights cells by cos(lat).
solve.py the code that made it
report.md what it did and what it means
Any language, method and file layout
a. Compare with the reference under every reading
64 combinations computed. The numbers match only
b. Rerun the agent's own code
on the same data → same answer
on changed data (rain added, dips injected)
→ moves with the data, still an accepted reading
change = current − previous; regional mean inside
the cell range; "drier" follows from −4.2 mm
d. Judge: Claude Opus 5.5, exact quotations
Does the report say the same as the code and answer?
Does it overgeneralise? No: two issues, one box.
Does it credit the data, the brief, its own choices? Yes.
Same checks for every system; spec certified by 5 tests
Three of nine earlier attempts on this template placed the 7-day window one day early. The reference under that reading matched their numbers exactly,
so each failed with the pitfall named. On the seasonal task the judge, reading the code an agent cited for its calibration, found a defect that the numbers
had not isolated. Every outcome keeps its evidence. A second episode on another box can start from this submission.

Terms: a pitfall is a known wrong method with a computable wrong answer; a probe reruns the agent's code on changed data; the controller is the trusted program that runs the agent, holds the references and runs the checks.
